title: Ensemble-disagreement gate: size inversely to inter-model spread, not just distance from fair
summary: Current p_yes treats all 55% forecasts as equal, but a 55% where ensembles agree (spread 2%) vs disagree (spread 12%) have very different realized calibration. Hypothesis: would_bet PnL conditioned on ensemble_std tercile will show the low-std tercile positive or ~0 and the high-std tercile deeply negative, because disagreement is a proxy for regime novelty where the model's shrinkage fails. Mechanism: Kalshi temperature markets are thin; when models disagree the true distribution is wider than any single member, and the market mid partially prices this while our point estimate doesn't.
evidence: creative cycle; testable from existing decision logs IF ensemble member probs or std are logged
otherwise requires new logging: per-decision ensemble_std field
next: Check whether decision records already include ensemble member spread; if not, add ensemble_std to evidence logging, then re-score would_bet PnL by std tercile after ~200 new decisions.

title: Progressive NO ladder on far strikes: treat the tail as a portfolio, not per-cell bets
summary: Instead of evaluating each far-strike D3 NO cell independently (where n=43 and one 97c loss erases 9 wins), buy NO across ALL far strikes for the same event as a single package. Exactly one strike settles YES, so a ladder of k far strikes at avg 2c costs 2k cents and returns 100*(k-1) minus losses — the positions are anti-correlated by construction. Mechanism: per-cell variance is binomial and brutal at 97c downside; the ladder converts it into 'did the outcome land in our covered tail at all', a much lower-variance bet on the model's tail mass being right. Sizing: cover strikes whose summed model p_yes < X%, exit by holding to settlement (no mark-to-market risk on a package).
evidence: prior: hourly|NYCH|30-15|D3 NO +11.2c n=43 but 24% loss rate
testable offline: reconstruct per-event strike sets from /api/evidence decisions + settlements, simulate ladder PnL vs single-cell PnL
next: Offline simulation: group historical would_bet far-strike NO decisions by event_ticker, compute package PnL if all qualifying strikes bought at logged ask; compare Sharpe vs current per-cell selection.

title: Maker-only execution band: join-bid instead of crossing when half-spread eats >30% of modeled edge
summary: Daily half-spread is ~1.6c and much of the NO-side loss is execution cost. Proposal: when mean_edge_c < 4c, only join the bid (maker) and walk away unfilled; when edge >= 4c, cross the spread. Mechanism: at 1.6c half-spread, a 3c-edge taker trade keeps ~1.4c before fees, while the same trade filled as maker keeps ~3c+rebate — the fill-rate cost is real but the adverse-selection cost of crossing one-sided books (1452/4071 markets!) is worse. Testable now: /api/spread_decomp already separates spread cost; re-score would_bet with entry at bid instead of ask for two-sided markets to estimate the maker-fill PnL uplift, then estimate fill probability from quote persistence in snapshots.

one_sided=1452 vs two_sided=2619 markets

title: Cross-city relative value: same-temperature-distribution events priced inconsistently across cities
summary: NY HIGH mid shows +16c and Seattle/Phoenix HIGH mid mildly positive — but the interesting trade is the spread between cities. When two cities have similar ensemble forecast distributions for a daily HIGH bucket but different market prices (adjusting for climatological base rates), buy the cheap one / sell the expensive one. Mechanism: liquidity and attention concentrate on NYC; smaller-city books are priced by fewer participants with cruder models, so systematic cross-city mispricing should persist. The current cell system evaluates each city in isolation and cannot see this.
evidence: prior: NY HIGH mid +16.2c vs Seattle/Phoenix only mildly positive — suggests city-level pricing quality differs
testable: compare model_p vs market price gaps per city from existing decision logs; look for cities where gap is systematically one-sided
next: From evidence logs, compute per-city mean (model_p - market_p) on daily HIGH mid cells; if Seattle/Phoenix show larger persistent gaps than NY with positive realized PnL, propose a city-pair relative-value cell dimension.

title: Model-run-age interaction filter: stale-forecast decisions may be the hidden D1 bleed
summary: D1 mid-strike hourly is systematically broken (predicted 33-38% vs actual 11-18%). One untested hypothesis: D1 decisions are disproportionately made on stale model runs (forecast issued >6h before decision), while D2/D3 use fresher runs. As lead time shrinks, the information advantage of a fresh ensemble over the market grows; the market incorporates new data within minutes, our model only at run boundaries. Mechanism: the miscalibration is not in the strike bucket, it's in forecast_age. Testable if decision logs record model run timestamp; otherwise add forecast_age_min to evidence logging.
evidence: prior: D1 hourly cells win_rate 0.11-0.18 vs predicted 0.33-0.38
testable from existing data only if run timestamps logged; else requires new field forecast_age_min
next: Grep evidence records for model run timestamp fields; if absent, add forecast_age_min to logging. Then bin would_bet PnL by forecast_age (<2h, 2-6h, >6h) — expect monotone decay.

title: New logging: per-decision order-book context + counterfactual entries so structure ideas become testable
summary: Current evidence logs record the decision and outcome but not enough market context to test execution or structure ideas offline. Add to each logged decision: (1) best_bid/best_ask and depth at both sides at decision time, (2) full strike ladder prices for the event (enables ladder/relative-value simulation), (3) ensemble member probs or std (enables disagreement gating), (4) forecast run timestamp (enables staleness analysis), (5) counterfactual PnL columns: pnl_if_maker, pnl_if_held_to_settle vs pnl_if_exit_at_mid. Cost: a few KB per decision; benefit: every idea in this cycle becomes measurable without code changes to the scorer.
